# sing-box-vps Agent Index

Project: sing-box-vps
Purpose: one-script install and management tool for deploying sing-box on Linux VPS hosts.
Primary language: Bash.
Runtime source of truth: install.sh.
Remote verification: Docker-based, auto-builds sing-box-vps-verify image.
Agent protocol contract revision: 2026091205.

Script 2026091007 adds typed selector/urltest outbound-group contracts to the managed component generator, alongside the Tor/SSH contracts, TUN auto-route loop guard, durable crash recovery for managed advanced-component takeover/export/rebuild and CAS writes on top of the existing Hysteria v1/NaiveProxy/ShadowTLS adapters. Selector and URLTest records allow only their sing-box 1.14 member and group fields, require a non-empty unique outbound list, require selector `default` to name one of those members, bound URLTest `tolerance` to uint16, and expose only a redacted `member_count` in inventory. Tor records allow only the sing-box 1.14 `executable_path`, `extra_args`, `data_directory`, string-valued `torrc` map and Dial Fields; inventory reports `runtime_mode=external` or `embedded_unverified`, because embedded Tor requires a separately built `with_embedded_tor`+CGO binary. SSH records allow only the sing-box 1.14 SSH and Dial Fields, require password/private_key/private_key_path authentication, reject deprecated or unknown fields, and expose only `pinned`/`unverified` host-key status in metadata. An empty `host_key` remains upstream-compatible (sing-box accepts any host key) but is never presented as pinned. When an enabled TUN sets `auto_route=true`, generation adds `route.auto_detect_interface=true` unless an explicit safe `route.default_interface` or guard already exists; an explicit false guard without a default interface fails closed. This is a config-level guard, not a claim that host policy routing, nftables, or the transparent data plane is managed. Hysteria provides manual-TLS QUIC/UDP multi-instance and multi-user lifecycle, Agent-safe summaries, independent bandwidth/obfs/QUIC options, and per-user client outbound JSON; NaiveProxy provides manual-TLS TCP/UDP multi-instance and multi-user lifecycle, Agent-safe summaries, Naive/QUIC client options, and per-user client outbound JSON. ShadowTLS provides a composite ShadowTLS outer plus private loopback Mixed detour, v1/v2/v3 authentication, handshake mappings, and per-user outbound JSON. Hysteria v1 uses `auth_str` and a string obfs password; it is never flattened into Hysteria2 fields. Naive outbound requires an official `with_naive_outbound` build and runtime `libcronet.so`; its standard URI/QR/SubMan surfaces are intentionally unavailable. ShadowTLS has no lossless standard URI, QR, or SubMan path. Shared CAS lifecycle and menu/Agent integration preserve legacy AnyTLS ACME/provider and Hysteria2 ACME/provider state without lossy migration. Hysteria, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS have no standard URI or SubMan sync path. Plain VLESS remains unmanaged. HTTPUpgrade and WebSocket early data remain runtime-blocked. SOCKS outbound components now use a typed sing-box 1.14 server/version/auth, TCP/UDP network, UDP-over-TCP and shared Dial Field allowlist; deprecated `domain_strategy`, unknown fields, invalid versions/networks/ports and control characters are rejected before state/CAS or takeover publication, while credentials remain confined to sensitive component export. HTTP outbound components now enforce the sing-box 1.14 server/port/auth, TCP-only path/headers, outbound TLS (including nested ECH/uTLS/REALITY shapes), and shared Dial Field allowlist; unknown or deprecated nested fields and control characters fail before state/CAS or takeover publication, and credentials remain export-only. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091008 adds a typed Shadowsocks outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 method/password semantics with strict Base64 SS2022 16/32-byte keys, TCP/UDP network, SIP003 plugin, UDP-over-TCP, multiplex and shared Dial Fields. Unknown/deprecated fields, unsupported methods/plugins, malformed nested values and control characters fail before state/CAS or takeover publication; credentials remain export-only and core checks do not imply a remote Shadowsocks handshake or data plane. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091008 also adds typed VMess and Trojan outbound component contracts: fixed 1.14 authentication, TCP/UDP network, outbound TLS, V2Ray transport, multiplex and shared Dial Fields. VMess preserves UUID/security/alter_id/packet encoding; Trojan preserves password. HTTP, WebSocket without early data, gRPC and TLS-only QUIC are accepted through the guarded transport validator, while HTTPUpgrade, WebSocket early data, plaintext QUIC and lite-gRPC `permit_without_stream` are rejected before state/CAS or takeover publication. Credentials remain export-only; two-core `check` evidence is local configuration evidence, not remote handshake or data-plane proof. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091009 adds a typed VLESS outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 UUID/flow/network/packet-encoding semantics, outbound TLS, guarded V2Ray transport, multiplex and shared Dial Fields. The empty flow supports native HTTP, WebSocket without early data, gRPC and TLS-only QUIC; `xtls-rprx-vision` requires enabled TLS and no V2Ray transport, while HTTPUpgrade, WebSocket early data, plaintext QUIC and lite-gRPC `permit_without_stream` fail closed before state/CAS or takeover publication. Omitted `packet_encoding` preserves the upstream xudp default. Credentials remain export-only; local target-core `check` evidence does not imply a remote VLESS handshake or data plane. This supersedes the earlier plain VLESS outbound limitation and does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091010 adds a typed AnyTLS outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 `AnyTLSOutboundOptions` requires `server`, `server_port`, a non-empty `password`, and enabled outbound TLS; optional session tuning and `client_metadata` retain their upstream scalar types, while shared Dial Fields remain bounded. AnyTLS has no configurable `network`, transport, or multiplex field, and `tcp_fast_open=true` is rejected because the target adapter cannot safely use it. Credentials remain export-only; two-core `check` evidence is local configuration evidence, not a remote AnyTLS handshake or TCP/UDP data-plane result. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091011 adds a typed Snell outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 `SnellOutboundOptions` accepts only version 4 (HTTP obfuscation) or 6 (traffic shaping), with typed PSK/userkey/reuse, TCP/UDP network, and shared Dial Fields. Version-crossed fields fail closed; v6 PSKs require at least 12 bytes, Snell v5 QUIC proxy is not exposed as a separate outbound, and UDP uses the protocol's TCP packet API. Credentials remain export-only; 1.14 core `check` evidence does not imply a remote Snell handshake or TCP/UDP data plane, while 1.13.18 explicitly lacks the type. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091111 adds a managed Snell v6 TCP data-plane probe to the Docker coexistence scenario. The probe validates the active schema-2 marker and schema-1 typed store, reuses the production Snell outbound exporter, runs the fixed 1.14.0 client after `sing-box check`, and reads an exact HTTP marker through the local SOCKS listener; the scenario keeps Snell's UDP packet API explicitly outside the separately measured native-UDP artifacts. Docker run `dev/verification-runs/20260911230518` records 15/15 scenarios and 25 regular protocol results: 24/24 executable probes succeed and one existing TUIC result is `unsupported`; the seven prior UDP artifacts remain successful. This is isolated container/loopback evidence, not public reachability, production deployment, external authentication, or proof that the full protocol goal is complete.

Script 2026091201 extends the NaiveProxy runtime transaction: official `libcronet.so` and its marker are staged atomically, captured in core-upgrade manifests, restored with the binary on config/check/service failure, and protected from overwriting or removing unowned libraries. The fixed 1.14.0 Docker TCP probe, strict rendered-config comparison, TLS/HTTP2 path and HTTP marker passed in runs `20260912014158` and `20260912022837`; UDP/HTTP3 and external deployment remain unverified.

Script 2026091202 proves the managed HTTP outbound data plane in Docker: `multi_protocol_coexistence` creates an authenticated loopback HTTP proxy, routes a SOCKS5 CONNECT through the typed HTTP outbound, and verifies exact proxy credentials, the `X-SBV-Proxy` header, rendered route and marker response; `http-outbound.result.env` is `RESULT=success` in run `20260912051138`. Agent JSON commands now keep stdout to one envelope and send progress logs to stderr, while component regeneration restores live advanced-route/Warp toggles before rendering. Local regression covers both boundaries; evidence remains fixed-core/loopback and does not imply public reachability, external proxy access, production deployment, or completion of the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091203 adds direct inbound override validation and a Docker data-plane proof. Direct component records now constrain `network` to `tcp`/`udp`, require safe non-empty `override_address` when present, and bound `override_port` to 1-65535. The coexistence scenario creates loopback TCP and UDP direct components, passes the target 1.14.0 `check`, then sends HTTP and UDP requests through the managed listeners to disposable loopback marker/echo fixtures; rendered config, listener snapshots, exact responses and both `direct-inbound.result.env` files are retained. This is isolated TCP/UDP override evidence only; transparent routing, host firewall policy, public deployment and the full protocol goal remain unverified.

Script 2026091204 tightens the advanced inbound state contract to the sing-box 1.14 `ListenOptions`, Direct/Redirect/TProxy network and UDP-NAT fields, TUN route/DNS/UID/package/MAC/platform fields, and Cloudflared token/HA/protocol/dialer fields. Unknown/deprecated fields, duplicate Direct/TProxy networks, malformed UID ranges, invalid enum/mark/port values and enabled TUN HTTP proxies without a server are rejected before CAS publication; target-core `check` remains the final address/duration semantic check. This typed state coverage does not claim host TUN devices, policy routing/nftables, transparent data-plane, Cloudflared control connection or full protocol completion.

Script 2026091205 adds a typed component route-rule contract. Component-owned route rules now accept the sing-box 1.14 default/logical matcher union and supported route actions with bounded scalar/listable fields; logical child rules are match-only and recursion is bounded. Unknown rule fields/actions, object-valued matchers, duplicate list members and invalid action-specific combinations fail before state/CAS or live takeover, while valid rules render unchanged. This closes the arbitrary route JSON passthrough gap without claiming host policy-routing, nftables, transparent data-plane or full protocol completion.

The current component transaction also performs a TUN resource postcheck after restarting an already-active service. If the candidate contains TUN, every core-owned interface must be present; auto-route must expose its iproute2 rule/table/route and auto-redirect must expose an nftables ruleset. Missing resources roll back applied managed firewall changes and restore the prior state/config/service with `transparent_resource_check_failed`; Redirect/TProxy host policy remains explicitly unowned.

Script 2026091101 adds a typed Hysteria2 outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 `Hysteria2OutboundOptions` covers server with mutually exclusive server-port or server-port ranges, port hopping, bandwidth, salamander/gecko obfs, TCP/UDP network, required outbound TLS, QUIC fields, BBR profile, Chrome QUIC control, Shared Dial Fields and the optional Hysteria Realm rendezvous object. Realm server/STUN/port-mapping/HTTP-client shapes and the distinction from Hysteria v1 fields fail closed before state/CAS or takeover publication. Credentials remain export-only; target-core `check` does not prove a remote QUIC handshake or UDP data plane. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091102 adds a typed Hysteria v1 outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 `HysteriaOutboundOptions` preserves server-port/range selection, hop interval, network-byte and Mbps bandwidth forms, string obfs, auth/auth_str, TCP/UDP network, required outbound TLS, QUIC fields and Shared Dial Fields. Hysteria v1 deprecated receive-window aliases and Hysteria2-only password/obfs/BBR/Realm fields fail closed before state/CAS or takeover publication. Credentials remain export-only; 1.14 full and 1.13 compatible-subset `check` evidence does not prove a remote Hysteria handshake or UDP data plane. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091103 adds a typed TUIC outbound component contract: fixed 1.14 `TUICOutboundOptions` preserves server/port, UUID/password, congestion control, native/quic UDP relay, optional UDP-over-stream, zero-RTT, heartbeat, TCP/UDP network, required outbound TLS, QUIC fields and Shared Dial Fields. `udp_relay_mode` and `udp_over_stream` conflicts fail closed before state/CAS or takeover publication; 1.13.18-compatible records omit the newer QUIC fields. Credentials remain export-only; 1.14 full and 1.13 compatible-subset `check` evidence does not prove a remote TUIC handshake or UDP data plane. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091104 adds typed NaiveProxy and ShadowTLS outbound component contracts: Naive preserves server/port, username/password, extra headers, HTTP/2 or QUIC, UDP-over-TCP, receive windows, the documented restricted TLS fields and shared Dial Fields; QUIC with non-zero insecure concurrency, unsupported TLS options, malformed UoT/header/window values and unknown/deprecated fields fail closed before state/CAS or takeover publication. ShadowTLS preserves the TCP-only wrapper's server/port, versions 1-3, password, required outbound TLS and shared Dial Fields, while remaining separate from the local outer-plus-loopback-Mixed inbound composite. Naive still requires `with_naive_outbound` plus runtime `libcronet.so`; 1.14 full and 1.13-compatible Naive/ShadowTLS `check` evidence is configuration-only and does not prove library loading, remote handshakes or data planes. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091105 adds a typed modern WireGuard endpoint contract: exact 32-byte standard Base64 private/public/PSK keys, CIDR address and allowed-IP validation, peer keepalive/reserved tuples, MTU/listen/workers, UDP NAT and shared Dial Fields are checked before state/CAS or takeover publication. The removed WireGuard outbound remains rejected; fixed 1.14 full-field and 1.13.18 base-subset `check` evidence does not prove system-interface permissions, peer handshake, or UDP data-plane operation. This increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Script 2026091106 adds typed Tailscale, OpenConnect, and OpenVPN client/server endpoint contracts. Tailscale state validates route prefixes, relay AddrPort values, exit-node conflicts, SSH options and shared Dial Fields; OpenConnect validates client-only flavor/token/mobile/TNCC/TLS/form shapes and keepalive/compression conflicts; OpenVPN validates TLS/static-key unions, remote/address families, certificate/key material, control wrapping, users and pushed DNS/routes. Material fields accept PEM/newline content while paths and non-material strings remain control-character safe. State/CAS and takeover tests cover render and malformed combinations; fixed-core checks and external control-plane/data-plane authentication remain configuration-only and unverified, so this increment does not complete the full protocol goal.

Advanced components are stored in `/root/sing-box-vps/components.json` (schema 1, independent revision). `sbv agent component list --json` is metadata-only; `sbv agent component diagnose --json` is a read-only health snapshot for state, config graph/listener/core checks, service state and managed firewall ledger; `sbv agent component export --json --id ID [--expected-revision N]` returns one complete sensitive record for a trusted caller; `sbv agent component takeover --json --yes --expected-revision N [--allow-public]` imports all registered advanced inbounds/endpoints and custom outbounds/groups from the live configuration, preserving object fields and route rules, and rejects any candidate that would drop an existing object or rule; built-in `direct`/`block` and generator-owned `warp-ep` endpoint remain generated defaults. Unknown outbound types, reserved tag conflicts and unowned global route rules remain fail-closed. SSH component records enforce the 1.14 SSH/Dial Field allowlist and at least one password/private-key/path credential; list/diagnose redact values and report only `host_key_verification=pinned|unverified`. Enabled TUN `auto_route` candidates receive `route.auto_detect_interface=true`; an existing explicit false guard without `route.default_interface` is rejected, and this does not claim host policy-routing/nftables ownership. When an active component transaction restarts a service whose candidate contains TUN, the same core-owned resource observation is a postcheck; missing interface/rule/route/nftables state rolls back applied managed firewall changes and restores the prior state/config/service with `transparent_resource_check_failed`. `sbv agent component rebuild --json --yes --expected-revision N` re-renders the same component revision through the normal validated candidate/resource/service rollback path. If a process is interrupted after the publish/resource journal is durable, `sbv agent component recover --json --yes --expected-revision N` validates the owner, phase, snapshot and firewall journal before rolling back; untrusted or active journals remain untouched. List/diagnose redact all config values. `create`/`replace`/`delete` require `--yes` plus an exact `--expected-revision`, use reference-protected CAS, and rebuild the combined config through graph validation, listener-resource validation, and the target `sing-box check`. The registry covers direct/tun/redirect/tproxy/cloudflared inbounds, WireGuard/Tailscale/OpenConnect/OpenVPN endpoints, and SSH/Tor/direct/bridge/selector/urltest/block plus protocol outbounds. Non-loopback listeners, TUN, tunnels, and OpenVPN server require `--allow-public`. Registry `implemented`, static `available`, per-read `environment.status`, and `validated` remain separate: environment observations report target-core/platform/dependency state but do not prove external authentication, routes/firewall, or a data plane. Component lifecycle is not a share-link or SubMan surface, and Cloudflared tokens never appear in list/status/diagnose output.

The component environment observation now parses the target binary's `Tags:` line. Conditional components report a missing required tag as `unavailable`; wrappers that omit the line remain `not_assessed`. The tag list is exposed only as validated metadata under `environment.core.build_tags`, and this does not prove external authentication, host routes/firewall or a data plane.

`component diagnose --json` also emits a read-only `transparent_resources`
snapshot. When the service is active it checks managed TUN interface,
iproute2 rule/route and auto-redirect nftables observations; missing core-owned
resources are reported as `unavailable`. Redirect/TProxy entries remain
`host_policy_rules_not_managed` because the installer does not claim ownership
of host PREROUTING or policy-routing rules. This is observation evidence only,
not a transparent data-plane or host-resource transaction claim.

Canonical documents:
- AGENTS.md: repository rules, validation requirements, SSH alias conventions, version rules.
- README.md: user-facing install, features, versions, runtime paths.
- docs/agents/sing-box-vps-agent-runbook.md: AI agent operations manual for repository maintenance, test VPS validation, production plans, install, upgrade, troubleshooting, and rollback.
- docs/agents/sing-box-1.13-to-1.14-upgrade-test.md: Hermes single-host fixed-version rehearsal with evidence and stop gates.
- skills/sing-box-vps-operator/SKILL.md: AgentSkills-style triggerable skill for Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, and similar agents.
- dev/verification/run.sh: local and remote verification entrypoint.
- dev/verification/docker/Dockerfile: Docker verification image definition.

Key runtime paths:
- /root/sing-box-vps/
- /root/sing-box-vps/config.json
- /root/sing-box-vps/protocols/
- /root/sing-box-vps-backups/ (root-only Agent upgrade backups; sensitive)
- /usr/local/bin/sbv
- systemd service: sing-box

Agent CLI:

- Trojan uses protocol ID trojan and menu preset 8 with schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. It supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate. client_trust is explicitly certificate or system. Only TLS system trust with losslessly representable transport can be shared as a SubMan URI; other users receive structured skip warnings. Client JSON preserves credentials and carries public certificate trust when selected, never the server private key. Native/HTTP/WS/gRPC use TCP listeners; TLS QUIC uses UDP listeners while retaining TCP and UDP business traffic. See the Trojan typed instance contract in the runbook.

- VMess uses protocol ID vmess and menu preset 9 (management menu 22) with schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. It supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with 1–128 unique users, `security`, `alter_id`, explicit `client_trust`, and none/http/ws/grpc/quic typed transports. Client JSON and `vmess://` links preserve credentials and representable transport fields, never the server private key. Only TLS system trust with losslessly representable transport can be shared as a SubMan URI; other users receive structured skip warnings. Native/HTTP/WS/gRPC use TCP listeners; TLS QUIC uses UDP listeners while retaining TCP and UDP business traffic. See the VMess typed instance contract in the runbook.
- AnyTLS uses protocol/state/Agent ID `anytls`, preset 4 and management menu 24 with a schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. It supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with 1–128 unique users, mandatory manual TLS paths and explicit `client_trust` (`certificate` or `system`). Client JSON and Agent links preserve per-user passwords, set `client_metadata` to an empty string, embed only public certificate PEM when selected, and never emit a private key; links also return `anytls_standard_uri_unavailable` because no standard URI is lossless. ACME/provider live AnyTLS remains on the legacy path and is rejected by typed takeover rather than flattened. See the AnyTLS typed instance contract in the runbook.

- Hysteria2 uses protocol/state/Agent ID `hy2`, preset 3 and management menu 25 with a schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. The typed path supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with 1–128 unique users, manual TLS, independently bounded `up_mbps`/`down_mbps`, salamander obfs and bounded masquerade. Agent links and client export preserve per-user credentials and public certificate trust only; Ed25519 certificates add a compatibility warning and no private key is emitted. Hysteria2 URI/SubMan output is system-trust only; certificate trust is skipped with a structured reason and partial options retain warnings. Legacy ACME/provider Hysteria2 remains untouched and is rejected by typed takeover rather than flattened. See the Hysteria2 typed instance contract in the runbook.

- Hysteria v1 uses protocol/state/Agent ID `hysteria`, registry preset 13 and management menu 28 with a schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. The typed path supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with 1–128 unique `name`/`auth_str` users, mandatory manual TLS, explicit `client_trust`, independent `up_mbps`/`down_mbps`, string obfs, and typed QUIC options. Server inbounds are UDP/QUIC with h3 TLS; client JSON exports one Hysteria outbound per user with `auth_str`, bandwidth, optional obfs password and QUIC fields. Links return `hysteria_standard_uri_unavailable`; Hysteria is never sent to SubMan. See the Hysteria typed instance contract in the runbook.

- TUIC uses protocol/state/Agent ID `tuic`, registry preset 12 and management menu 27 with a schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. The typed path supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with 1–128 unique UUID/password users, mandatory manual TLS, explicit `client_trust`, and congestion/auth-timeout/heartbeat/zero-rtt options. Server inbounds are UDP/QUIC with h3 TLS; client JSON exports one TUIC outbound per user with `network:["tcp","udp"]`. `udp_relay_mode` (`native|quic`) and `udp_over_stream` are outbound-only. Links return `tuic_standard_uri_unavailable`; TUIC is never sent to SubMan. See the TUIC typed instance contract in the runbook.

- NaiveProxy uses protocol/state/Agent ID `naive`, registry preset 14 and management menu 29 with a schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. The typed path supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with 1–128 unique username/password users, mandatory manual TLS, explicit `client_trust`, TCP/UDP listener selection, and bounded Naive/QUIC options. Server inbounds render the selected network; client JSON exports one Naive outbound per user. Links return `naive_standard_uri_unavailable` and `naive_libcronet_required`; NaiveProxy is never sent to SubMan. See the NaiveProxy typed instance contract in the runbook.

- ShadowTLS uses protocol/state/Agent ID `shadowtls`, registry preset 15 and management menu 30 with a schema-1 JSON store and schema-2 active marker. Each typed instance renders one ShadowTLS outer listener plus one private loopback Mixed detour; v1 has no credentials, v2 has one password, and v3 has 1–128 unique users. The typed path supports create/replace/delete/default/recover, not legacy migrate, with handshake/SNI mappings, v3 strict/wildcard settings, explicit client trust, and complete per-user outbound JSON. Links return `shadowtls_standard_uri_unavailable`; ShadowTLS is never sent to SubMan. See the ShadowTLS typed instance contract in the runbook.

- Standalone HTTP uses protocol ID http, menu preset 6, and the shared schema-2 instance lifecycle (create/replace/delete/default/recover, never migrate). Typed records additionally require tls: {enabled:false} or {enabled:true,server_name,certificate_path,key_path}. HTTP CONNECT client export is TCP-only; TLS export embeds public certificate trust, never the server key. TLS URI material is unavailable with http_tls_uri_unrepresentable: use export-client JSON. No HTTP SubMan sync. Existing Mixed/SOCKS formats are unchanged.
- Shadowsocks uses public protocol/Agent ID `shadowsocks`, alias `ss`, registry/menu preset 7, and the shared schema-2 instance lifecycle (create/replace/delete/default/recover, never migrate). Its typed schema-1 JSON store requires `listen.network` and an `authentication` object; the exact record and method/network limits are documented in the runbook below. New listeners default to loopback; a non-loopback write requires `--allow-public` (interactive management asks for the same consent). The `none` method emits a plaintext warning. Final evidence for this contract includes final script hash `8d24fa6e`, two core targets, all 9 methods in config checks, four native Bash/Bash 4.2 runtime groups across 1.13.18 and 1.14 with 7 TCP plus 7 UDP cases per group, and long-PSK derivation. The Docker rerun recorded 12/12 scenarios, 18/18 TCP probes, successful `rolled_back` and `success` rollback outcomes, and matching script/container hashes; see the runbook for the local-test boundary.

- Mixed/SOCKS share URI userinfo is percent-encoded byte-for-byte. For Mixed credentials that HTTP Basic cannot represent (colon in username or ASCII control characters), links omits HTTP and returns mixed_http_auth_unrepresentable without changing credentials; SOCKS5 remains available. socks5_uri_transport_options_omitted warns that the URI does not carry UoT v2 options: use export-client JSON for full configuration. Encoding is not encryption.
- sbv agent capabilities --json: machine-readable capability matrix; read-only, no secrets.
- sbv agent upgrade-check --json 1.14.0: read-only eligibility preflight that does not reconcile or migrate state; inspect ready, blockers, config hash/schema, legacy fields, and warnings. It does not download the target binary.
- sbv agent upgrade --json 1.14.0 --yes: guarded binary upgrade; mutating and service-impacting, with automatic backup under /root/sing-box-vps-backups/, a manifest covering every regular runtime file plus control files, and an atomic transaction-result.json audit record.
- sbv agent status --json: service/version/paths/protocols plus network stacks, BBR, REALITY/QoS counts, and integration presence.
- sbv agent nodes --json: log-safe summaries for every protocol and every REALITY/Mixed/SOCKS/HTTP/Shadowsocks/Trojan/VMess/Hysteria2/Hysteria v1/AnyTLS/Snell/TUIC/NaiveProxy/ShadowTLS instance, including instance revision without credentials. For Shadowsocks, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS authentication, expose only bounded metadata; never expose server or user keys/passwords/UUIDs/`auth_str`.
- sbv agent links --json: full per-protocol and per-REALITY/Mixed/SOCKS/HTTP/Shadowsocks/Trojan/VMess/Hysteria2/Hysteria v1/AnyTLS/Snell/TUIC/NaiveProxy/ShadowTLS-instance connection material; treat output as sensitive. Shadowsocks returns `links` keyed by stable outbound tag, an `outbounds` array and `warnings`; VMess returns matching `vmess://` links and outbounds; Hysteria2 returns per-user `hy2://` links/outbounds plus trust, Ed25519 and partial-option warnings; Hysteria v1 returns per-user outbound JSON, `links:{}` and `hysteria_standard_uri_unavailable`; AnyTLS returns per-user outbounds, `links:{}` and `anytls_standard_uri_unavailable`; Snell returns per-user outbound JSON, `links:{}` and `snell_standard_uri_unavailable`; TUIC returns per-user outbound JSON, `links:{}` and `tuic_standard_uri_unavailable`; NaiveProxy returns per-user outbound JSON, `links:{}`, `naive_standard_uri_unavailable` and `naive_libcronet_required`; ShadowTLS returns per-user outbound JSON, `links:{}`, and `shadowtls_standard_uri_unavailable`. Long 2022 PSKs remain unchanged in the store, while client-equivalent SHA-256-derived keys carry `shadowsocks_2022_psk_derived`.
- sbv agent export-client --json: generate and validate /root/sing-box-vps/client/sing-box-client.json without changing the running server config.
- sbv agent check --json: run sing-box check against the server config and return structured stdout/stderr/status.
- sbv agent doctor --json: read-only diagnostics with service, paths, protocols, and embedded config check.
- sbv agent warp --json: read-only Warp/account/routing summary.
- sbv agent service restart --json --yes: guarded restart after config validation; production use requires approval.
- sbv agent subman-sync --json: non-interactive SubMan node push; treat as sensitive and require configured /root/sing-box-vps/subman.env.

Capability safety labels:
- read-only: status, capabilities, upgrade-check, check, doctor, nodes, warp.
- mutating: upgrade, service restart, export-client, subman-sync, component takeover/rebuild/create/replace/delete.
- sensitive: links, export-client, subman-sync, component export; these may expose usable credentials or external node data.
- instance <operation> socks|http|shadowsocks|trojan|vmess|hy2|hysteria|anytls|snell|tuic|naive|shadowtls: mutating, service-impacting and revision/CAS guarded. The typed SOCKS, HTTP, Shadowsocks, Trojan, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS lifecycle surfaces are covered by the recorded focused evidence; this does not mean the full protocol goal is complete.
- interactive-only: fresh install, protocol changes, REALITY instance/QoS changes, Warp changes, BBR/system changes, media checks, takeover/repair, uninstall.

Capability domains to preserve in documentation and tests:
- protocols: VLESS REALITY, Mixed HTTP/SOCKS, standalone SOCKS, standalone HTTP, Shadowsocks, Trojan, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, ShadowTLS, coexistence; each listed surface remains bounded by its documented fields and evidence.
- REALITY: multi-instance, per-instance port/ShortID/name/outbound, upload/download QoS.
- TLS: ACME HTTP-01, Cloudflare DNS-01, manual certificates, Hysteria2 Ed25519 client warning.
- routing/system: Warp all/selective routing, custom and local/remote rule sets, IPv4/IPv6/dual stack, DNS/outbound strategy, BBR.
- operations: service lifecycle/logs, node/link/QR output, client export, SubMan, takeover/repair, core/script upgrade, core/script uninstall, typed Hysteria/Snell/TUIC/NaiveProxy/ShadowTLS instance transactions.

SSH aliases:
- sing-box-test: test VPS for validation.
- sing-box-prod: production VPS. Production-changing commands require a plan and explicit approval first.

Important requirements:
- Run sing-box check after modifying or generating sing-box server or client configs.
- Back up existing runtime configuration before changing production state.
- Docker-based remote verification: see dev/verification/run.sh and dev/verification/docker/Dockerfile.
- Run bash dev/verification/run.sh after changes to install.sh, uninstall.sh, configs/, utils/, or dev/verification/.
- Do not reveal secrets, private keys, passwords, tokens, full node links, or QR payloads unless explicitly requested and safe.
- Treat sbv agent links --json, export-client --json, and subman-sync --json as sensitive connection-material commands.
- Upgrade backups contain the full runtime state and must never be copied into shared logs or artifacts.
- Agent JSON uses schema_version "1.0" with the legacy schema "1" retained. For upgrades that change the installed version, require transaction.result_persisted=true and inspect transaction.result_path, status, manifest hash, and rollback result. If the target version is already installed, accept only changed=false with transaction.status=not_attempted and transaction.reason=already_installed; no backup or transaction result file is created.
- Do not run production install, upgrade, restart, stop, uninstall, purge, firewall mutation, or config overwrite without an approved production operation plan.

Common task routing:
- Fresh install on new VPS: read README.md and docs/agents/sing-box-vps-agent-runbook.md.
- Upgrade existing VPS: read docs/agents/sing-box-vps-agent-runbook.md, then prepare a production operation plan for sing-box-prod.
- Hermes 1.13 to 1.14 rehearsal: first update sbv, then read docs/agents/sing-box-1.13-to-1.14-upgrade-test.md and run its preflight/evidence gates before any core mutation.
- Test remote verification: read dev/verification/run.sh, dev/verification/common.sh, and AGENTS.md.
- Production troubleshooting: use read-only checks first, then prepare a production operation plan for changes.
- AI agent node info retrieval: prefer sbv agent nodes --json for summaries and sbv agent links --json only in trusted contexts.
- VLESS REALITY multi-instance or rate-limit work: use script-managed state under /root/sing-box-vps/protocols/vless-reality.d/ and /root/sing-box-vps/reality-qos.filters; do not hand-edit generated config.json.
- REALITY takeover retains existing instance IDs, names, QoS and the default instance by matching saved inbound tags. Connection parameters follow the live config; an old public key is retained only when its private key matches. Ambiguous saved tags stop reconstruction before state replacement.
- Instance reads use the shared protocol/instance adapter. Legacy singleton state is exposed internally as main; REALITY keeps its existing multi-instance IDs, while Mixed, standalone SOCKS, HTTP, Shadowsocks, Trojan, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS use active schema-2 markers with JSON stores whose `schema_version` is 1, and expose instance revisions. Agent reads and client rendering do not migrate legacy state or create credentials.
- The typed stores under protocols/instances/ now have Mixed, standalone SOCKS, HTTP, Shadowsocks, Trojan, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS handlers. Mixed supports `sbv agent instance create|replace|delete|default|migrate|recover mixed --json --yes --expected-revision N`; SOCKS, HTTP, Shadowsocks, Trojan, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS support the same commands except `migrate`, which is rejected because they have no legacy `.env` migration path (existing live configuration uses takeover; AnyTLS, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS only take over their typed subsets). Create/replace require a complete private `--file` record, delete/default require `--id`, and recover requires the original journal revision. Shadowsocks, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS records describe only their documented typed inbound shape; do not add relay, mux, plugin, realm, STUN or other unmodeled field claims. The typed lifecycle/runtime/export surfaces are covered by the recorded focused evidence, while the full protocol goal remains bounded and unfinished. See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-06-unified-protocol-management.md` for the evidence boundary.
- Resource preflight is `managed_listener_plan <config_file>`: the JSON array is owner-tag/protocol-state/address-family/transport/port/dual-stack keyed and is driven by the registered Mixed/SOCKS/HTTP/Shadowsocks/Trojan/VMess/Hysteria2/Hysteria v1/Snell/TUIC/NaiveProxy/ShadowTLS `listen_networks`. It rejects unknown types and `netns`/`bind_interface`/`reuse_addr`; broad existing firewall rules are not an ownership ledger. Active schema-2 Shadowsocks/VMess/Hysteria2/Hysteria v1/Snell/TUIC/NaiveProxy/ShadowTLS removal is already short-circuited to its instance-management delete path; preserve that guard so legacy port-only cleanup is not used for structured stores. SubMan has dedicated SS, VMess and Hysteria2 paths: only encrypted dual-network SS and losslessly representable TLS/system-trust VMess/Hysteria2 entries are syncable, while unsupported entries are skipped. Hysteria v1, Snell, AnyTLS, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS have no SubMan path. Trojan, VMess, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS project their actual listener from typed transport/config, not from the registry's possible-network union.
- Server candidates and typed stores reject overlapping managed fixed listeners before publication. Firewall cleanup compares the previous config backup with remaining listeners, retaining referenced transport/port rules. Missing or unmodelled inventories block cleanup; backend failure is nonzero and may leave partial external changes. This is reference protection, not proof of ownership of existing firewall rules or a complete system-resource rollback.
- Firewall opening reads the complete committed listener plan and opens only registered listening transports. Full protocol removal requires a successful stop and confirmed inactive service before clearing config/index and rules. Post-publication opening failure reports config_committed, firewall_may_be_partial and service_restart_not_attempted; inspect the service manually rather than assuming rollback.
- Client export: use sbv agent export-client --json and remember it writes /root/sing-box-vps/client/sing-box-client.json with backup/validation. Mixed and standalone SOCKS export as SOCKS5 with UoT v2; Shadowsocks export preserves its typed network and authentication in full JSON; Trojan, VMess, ordinary VLESS, Hysteria2, Hysteria v1, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS export one full outbound per user with transport and explicit public-certificate/system trust where applicable. Authentication is preserved, never generated or silently disabled. AnyTLS sets `client_metadata` empty and has no lossless URI; Hysteria2 emits independent bandwidth/obfs fields and warns for Ed25519 certificates; Hysteria v1 emits independent bandwidth/obfs/QUIC fields; Snell maps inbound v5 to outbound v4 and inbound v6 to outbound v6 and preserves v5 obfs host or v6 shaping; TUIC preserves congestion, heartbeat, zero-rtt and outbound-only relay/udp-over-stream; NaiveProxy preserves TLS, QUIC, stream-window and header options but requires `with_naive_outbound` and `libcronet.so`; ShadowTLS preserves its version, handshake, trust, and per-user credentials in full outbound JSON. Missing/invalid port or auth state blocks the whole export without replacing the existing file/backup. Plaintext transport warnings require a trusted network or protected tunnel. UoT is not encryption. Never export a private key or disable verification.
- SubMan sync: use sbv agent subman-sync --json only when SubMan config exists and the target context is trusted. Shadowsocks has a dedicated integration for encrypted SIP002-representable dual-network entries; single-network entries are skipped because SIP002 cannot preserve the restriction, and `none` with an empty password is rejected by the current parser and skipped with `shadowsocks_subman_none_unsupported`. Trojan, VMess and Hysteria2 use dedicated multi-instance, per-user paths: only lossless TLS/system-trust URIs are eligible; plaintext, certificate trust, unrepresentable transport, partial options and oversized URIs retain explicit skipped counts/warnings, including when every user is skipped. Hysteria v1, Snell, AnyTLS, TUIC, NaiveProxy, and ShadowTLS have no standard URI or SubMan adapter and are always reported unsupported without a write request. Same-snapshot VMess and Hysteria2 mock coverage is local-only; no real sync has been performed without authorization.
- Repository maintenance: read AGENTS.md, affected scripts, and run verification as required.
- sing-box config syntax or migration: use Context7 first; fall back to official sing-box docs or repository only when needed.

Search keywords:
install, upgrade, production, Docker verification, rollback, recovery, sbv agent, node info, connection links, client export, SubMan sync, sing-box check, sing-box-prod, dev/verification/run.sh, config.json, protocols, Warp, VLESS REALITY, REALITY multi-instance, rate limits, QoS, Hysteria2, Hysteria, AnyTLS, Snell, TUIC, Mixed proxy, standalone SOCKS, systemctl sing-box.

Protocol registry:
- Client export candidates pass reference validation and the target core check before publication. `client_config_validation_failed` preserves the previous export and backup; diagnostics remain on stderr.
- `sbv agent capabilities --json` includes additive `protocol_registry` metadata from install.sh. Legacy `protocols` keys and envelope remain compatible.
- Separate family/preset/role/state_id/agent_id; legacy `vless` still resolves to the REALITY preset, Hysteria2 state ID remains `hy2` with typed management menu 25, standalone SOCKS is the fifth registry preset with menu order 5 and state/Agent ID `socks`, Shadowsocks is menu preset 7 with state/Agent ID `shadowsocks` and alias `ss`, Trojan is menu preset 8 with state/Agent ID `trojan` and management menu 21, VMess is menu preset 9 with state/Agent ID `vmess` and management menu 22, AnyTLS is preset 4 with state/Agent ID `anytls` and management menu 24, Snell is preset 11 with state/Agent ID `snell` and management menu 26, TUIC is preset 12 with state/Agent ID `tuic` and management menu 27, Hysteria v1 is preset 13 with state/Agent ID `hysteria` and management menu 28, NaiveProxy is preset 14 with state/Agent ID `naive` and management menu 29, and ShadowTLS is preset 15 with state/Agent ID `shadowtls` and management menu 30.
- `implemented` describes the project adapter; `available=null` and `validated.status=not_assessed` do not certify the current environment or connection. Perform instance preflight/check and inspect real probe artifacts.
- Script 2026091110 extends the real UDP payload probe to managed Trojan QUIC, TUIC, SS2022, VMess QUIC and ordinary VLESS QUIC, and fixes both the missing client `h3` ALPN required by the rendered TUIC server and the VMess/VLESS QUIC exporters' incorrect `network:["udp"]` restriction. The coexistence scenario creates typed Trojan QUIC, UUID/password TUIC, SS2022 TCP+UDP and VMess QUIC instances; the fresh ordinary-VLESS scenario replaces the same managed instance from TCP/none to TLS QUIC while retaining the `vless-plain` index identity. Fixed 1.14.0 clients send SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE markers through QUIC/native UDP to a local echo, and all seven UDP artifacts report `RESULT=success`. Docker run `dev/verification-runs/20260911215408` records 15/15 scenarios and 24 regular protocol results: 23/23 executable probes succeed and one existing TUIC result is `unsupported`. This remains isolated container/loopback evidence, not public reachability, production deployment, external authentication, or proof that the full protocol goal is complete.
- Unknown state IDs/schema versions and invalid builder fragments block reconstruction without removing those entries. Use a compatible script or restore a reviewed backup; do not delete unknown state to bypass the guard.
- Live inbound discovery is all-or-nothing. Unknown types, non-REALITY VLESS, duplicate single-instance protocols, or duplicate explicit tags make the instance incomplete and block reconciliation, takeover, regeneration, and partial Agent status/node/link output. The three Agent commands return `live_inbound_inventory_untrusted` without exposing a partial list. They also require an exact live-config/index set match and a complete base-state inventory, returning `protocol_index_untrusted` or `protocol_state_untrusted`; `nodes`/`links` additionally reject incomplete REALITY instance enumeration and discard rendered nodes if any later load or state restoration fails. This is an inbound-inventory guard, not proof that custom fields, outbounds, endpoints, or routes are losslessly managed.
- Full-scope progress: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-06-unified-protocol-management.md; upstream evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-protocol-coverage.md.
